entry.title: Independent Leakage Does Not Save Evasive LWE: Refuting Folklore Fixes in the Private-Coin Setting
entry.summary:
The evasive learning with errors (evasive LWE) assumption has enabled a wide range of advanced cryptographic constructions from lattices in the past few years. The simple intuition that LWE remains secure even when additional ``non-zeroizing'' short preimages are given has proved highly versatile in applications. Unfortunately, recent counterexamples have refuted its general private-coin formulations, showing that having the short preimages along with arbitrary auxiliary leakage about the secret and target matrices can invalidate this intuition.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum #combinatorics

entry.title: Superlattice methods for the shortest vector problem and discrete Gaussian sampling
entry.summary:
We give worst-case algorithms for the shortest vector problem (SVP) and discrete Gaussian sampling (DGS) at arbitrary widths. Both algorithms generate lists on a dense superlattice and combine vectors along a chain down to the input lattice. Random shifts let us control the expected number of representations of a vector regardless of the lattice.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum

entry.title: Masked Solving of Linear Equations System and Application to UOV Signatures
entry.summary:
In response to the looming quantum threat, NIST has selected four algorithms for standardization (i.e., ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, and FN-DSA), yet three of the four schemes are based on Euclidean lattices, which raises concerns about the mathematical diversity of post-quantum algorithms. NIST has therefore announced an additional call for post-quantum signatures with a preference for schemes constructed from assumptions other than lattices. Among such candidates, the Unbalanced Oil and Vinegar (UOV) signature over the multivariate quadratic (MQ) problem is attractive for its short signature and security against quantum cryptanalysis.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum
